clue.text: Holiday postponed? Give over!

blocks.note: leave is time off work, a holiday
an event that is off has been called off or put back

explanation.surface: Someone told their holiday is delayed shouts in exasperation for the speaker to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a holiday that is 'off' is a stretch of 'postponed'; the exclamation is the real meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal commands telling someone to stop doing something annoying.

clue.text: Boy may bring post up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: post and mail both mean letters delivered

explanation.surface: A lad might fetch the letters upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Liam is a common male first name, so it can stand for a boy.

clue.text: Evergreen song about a posh vehicle

indicators.note: about means going around, so the song wraps the other pieces

blocks.note: an aria is a song in an opera
taken as written
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U speech
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A timeless popular song about a smart motor car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evergreen' looks like a description of a lasting song, but it is the tree. U for upper-class comes from a 1950s essay sorting words into U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is a genus of coniferous trees, including the monkey puzzle, which keep their leaves all year.

clue.text: Finish with awfully sore back

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to finish is to end
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Ending the day with a terribly painful back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as a body part but is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a candidate or plan is to support it, which is what endorsing means.

clue.text: Dates to be avoided?

blocks.note: surface reading: calendar days or romantic outings best skipped
setter's reading: dates are a fruit, and fruit that must not be eaten is the kind Eve was banned from in Eden

explanation.walkthrough: Dates look like calendar days or social engagements, but they are the edible fruit of the date palm.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the fruit of the tree of knowledge that Adam and Eve were told not to eat, hence anything prohibited but tempting.

clue.text: Very silly hat for a daredevil

blocks.note: mad means crazy, very silly
a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A ridiculous piece of headgear worn by a stunt performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap is a reckless, impulsive person, much like a thrill-seeking risk-taker.

clue.text: Very old worker drinking nice bubbly

indicators.note: bubbly suggests fizzing and effervescing, so the letters are stirred around
drinking means taking in, so one word swallows the other

blocks.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An elderly employee sipping some pleasant champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' looks like the champagne the old worker is drinking, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means belonging to the distant past, extremely aged.

clue.text: Grasp cold fish

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Getting hold of a chilly fish from the slab.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to keep a tight grip on something, which is what grasping it means.

clue.text: Insecticide used in most of district, eco-friendly

indicators.note: most of means all but the end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a parish is a local district; most of it loses the final letter
green means environmentally friendly

explanation.surface: A pesticide applied across much of an area, yet claimed to be kind to the environment.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that the answer is a highly toxic arsenic compound, anything but green.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris green is a poisonous copper arsenite pigment once widely used to kill insects and rats.

clue.text: Sweet girl the kid shut out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A lovely girl whom the child locked outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet girl' reads as one phrase, but 'Sweet' alone is the definition, the confection.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkish delight is a confection of gel cubes dusted in sugar, a type of candy.

clue.text: Tony, say, a minor under court's protection

blocks.note: taken as written
a ward of court is a child placed under a court's protection

explanation.surface: A boy called Tony who is a minor placed in the care of the court.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony looks like a boy's name, but it is the Tony, the American theatre prize; 'say' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tony is a prize given for Broadway theatre, an example of a trophy or honour.

clue.text: Hurricane at sea could make one more coarse

indicators.note: something at sea is lost and confused, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A storm out on the ocean could make a sailor cruder in their language.
explanation.definitionFit: Raunchy means crude or bawdy, so the comparative form means more vulgar.

clue.text: Caught by a king (Richard), warrior king leaves town

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
R stands for rex, Latin for king
Rick is a short form of the name Richard
Fergus is the name of several legendary Irish and Scottish warrior kings

explanation.surface: A captured king Richard and a warrior monarch departing a town, like a scrap of medieval history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like departure but just links the wordplay to the definition, meaning 'results in'. Carrickfergus is a town on Belfast Lough in Northern Ireland, named after the king Fergus.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrickfergus is a historic town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland, famous for its Norman castle.

clue.text: A Derby winner, a winner with children?

blocks.note: first meaning: the racehorse that won the 1964 Epsom Derby
second meaning: the Christmas gift-bringer whom children adore

explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's great flat horse race, run at Epsom; one winner bore the name of the Christmas figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The racehorse won the Derby in 1964, and the festive gift-giver is hugely popular with youngsters.

clue.text: Broadcast by chief, an idiot

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
the head is the chief or leader

explanation.surface: A boss who goes on radio or television and is called a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is slang for a stupid, empty-headed person, a fool.

clue.text: A colonist needs to adjust, right?

blocks.note: to settle something is to fix or adjust it into place
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A question about whether a newcomer to a colony must adapt to new ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is a person who moves to a new land and establishes a home there, a pioneer.

clue.text: Litter strewn by one over centre of Bordeaux — take no immediate action

indicators.note: strewn means scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order
centre of points to the middle letters of the following word

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
I is the Roman numeral one
the two middle letters of the eight-letter city name

explanation.surface: Rubbish scattered around a Bordeaux square, and a decision to leave it for now.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'one over' the next piece means it sits above it, so I comes before DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To let it ride is an idiom meaning to leave a matter alone and see what happens.

clue.text: Item used in partial payment, rated terribly fashionable

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters come out wrongly ordered

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
in means in fashion

explanation.surface: An old car offered towards the cost of a new one is judged dreadfully trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is goods handed over to a seller as part of the price of something new.

clue.text: More on court selection

blocks.note: extra means more
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Extra time on a tennis court, with players chosen for a match.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage chosen from a longer text, an excerpt.

clue.text: Fan, mostly profound about poll

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: deep means profound; mostly leaves it without its final letter
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: A supporter who has deep thoughts about an election.
explanation.definitionFit: A devotee is an enthusiast or keen follower, the same as a fan.

clue.text: Opposing a gift for tramp

blocks.note: V is short for versus, against
taken as written
a grant is money given, a gift

explanation.surface: Someone objecting to handing out charity to a homeless person.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant is a homeless person who wanders, the same as a tramp or vagabond.

clue.text: Daily worry about fair part of holiday package, perhaps

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word for worry is read backwards

blocks.note: a daily or char is a cleaning woman who comes in each day
to fret is to worry
fair hair or skin is light in colour

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman fretting over one aspect of a package holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper or adjective, but in British usage a daily is a domestic cleaner, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: A charter flight, hired by a tour operator rather than scheduled, is often bundled into a package holiday.

clue.text: Liberal representative, no leader

indicators.note: having no leader means the first letter is taken away

blocks.note: a sample is a representative portion

explanation.surface: A Liberal Party MP left without a party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' with its capital looks like the political party, but it means generous.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberal helping is a generous one, plentiful in amount.

clue.text: Famous pianist — she's playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved about freely into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A celebrated concert pianist, and she is performing now.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Myra Hess was a British pianist famed for her wartime National Gallery concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Myra Hess was a renowned British concert pianist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Attractive draw at home against fourth in league

indicators.note: fourth in points to the letter in that position of the following word

blocks.note: a draw is an attraction, something with appeal
to be in is to be at home
the fourth letter of league

explanation.surface: A football team's draw at home against a side placed fourth in the league is pleasing.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture of a home draw hides that 'draw' means an attraction here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appealing has charm and draws people in, so it is attractive.

clue.text: Nimble porter? Good one inside

indicators.note: inside says these letters go within the word for porter

blocks.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
G is the abbreviation for good
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sprightly hotel porter, with a decent one working indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter looks like a person carrying bags, but it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile and nimble are synonyms for quick and light in movement.

clue.text: Nap in cosiest armchair

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Dozing off in the comfiest chair in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is a short afternoon sleep, so it is a snooze.

clue.text: Good man speaks, speaks haltingly

blocks.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
to utter is to speak

explanation.surface: A virtuous man talks, but stumbles over his words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good man' for ST, saint, is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stutters talks with involuntary repetitions and pauses, so their speech is broken.
